rationale: Class A quote-removal token merge: empty single-quote pair splits 'rm' so today's rm regex (needs 'rm' + whitespace adjacency) never matches -> today ALLOWs. Bash quote removal restores 'rm -rf /'. Sound evaluator canonicalizes r''m -> rm and DENIES. Red: today leaks a destructive command.

Class A backslash token merge: 'r\m' has no literal 'rm' adjacency so no BLOCKED_REGEX fires -> today ALLOWs. Bash backslash removal yields 'rm -rf /'. Evaluator canonicalizes to rm -rf / -> DENY. Red: destructive command leaks today.

Class A double-quote merge: 'rm"' is followed by a quote, not whitespace, so /rm\s+-r[f]?\s+\// misses -> today ALLOWs. Bash quote removal yields rm -rf /. Evaluator strips quotes -> DENY. Red: leaks today.

Class A: the '' before / breaks the '-rf /' adjacency the rm regexes require (char after '-rf ' is a quote, not /) -> today ALLOWs. Bash quote removal collapses ''/ to / giving rm -rf /. Evaluator -> DENY. Red.

Class A quote merge inside the flag: '-r''f' is not literal '-rf', so -r[f]? then \s+ fails to match (char after -r is a quote) -> today ALLOWs. Bash quote removal yields rm -rf /. Evaluator canonicalizes -r''f -> -rf -> DENY. Red.

Class B $IFS field-splitting: '$IFS' is literal text at match time so there is no whitespace after 'rm' -> rm regexes miss -> today ALLOWs. Bash expands $IFS to a space at exec, running rm -rf /. Evaluator treats unquoted $IFS as a field boundary -> argv [rm,-rf,/] -> DENY. Red.

Class B braced ${IFS} variant: same as B-1 -- literal ${IFS} means no whitespace after rm at match time -> today ALLOWs; bash expands to rm -rf / at exec. Evaluator field-splits on ${IFS} -> DENY. Red.

Class B $IFS obfuscation of a sensitive-path read. Today has NO path protection for Bash and no $IFS handling -> ALLOWs. A plain 'cat ~/.aws/credentials' is a lone read (dual-use -> ASK), but $IFS field-split obfuscation over a credentials path has no benign purpose, so the evaluator escalates the obfuscated sensitive read to DENY (deny-not-ask: obfuscated sensitive-read family). Red.

Class C command substitution: the binary is computed by $(echo rm); 'rm)' breaks adjacency so today ALLOWs. Evaluator recurses the substitution and sees a computed command name with destructive argv (-rf /) -> $CMD -rf / -> DENY (deny, not ask). Red.

Class C substitution INSIDE double quotes: rm -rf /etc/passwd is a subpath (not bare /) and lives in a $() the guard treats as inert text -> today ALLOWs. Evaluator recurses inside double quotes (the quoted-arg variant even Continue misses), inner verdict DENY -> most-restrictive -> DENY. Red.

Class C backtick substitution: inner rm -rf /etc is a subpath so regex2 (/rm...\/[^a-zA-Z]/) misses (/ followed by 'e') and regex1 needs / at EOS -> today ALLOWs. Evaluator extracts the backtick inner, recurses -> rm -rf /etc -> DENY. Red.

Class D decode->interpreter: today's regex is /base64\s+-d.../ which does NOT match '--decode' (second dash breaks -d) -> today ALLOWs. Decoder piped into a shell sink is unambiguous RCE -> evaluator DENY (not ask). Red: the --decode variant leaks today.

Class D decode->non-sh interpreter: today's regex requires the sink to be (bash|sh), so piping into python3 evades -> today ALLOWs. base64 -d into any interpreter sink is decode->RCE -> evaluator DENY (not ask). Red.

Class D genuine dual-use: a bare NON-decoded pipe into an interpreter -> ASK (could be a legit REPL feed). Today has no rule for it and returns null/ALLOW, so today's verdict (null) != expected (ask) -> WRONG -> Red. Reserved ASK per the deny-not-ask rule (no decoder, so not a bypass class).

Class E alt-argv destructive flag: 'find / -delete' recursively deletes from root but no BLOCKED pattern covers find -> today ALLOWs. Evaluator's per-binary/per-flag table (find -delete) -> DENY. Red.

Class E: today only blocks the literal 'dd if=/dev/zero' string and '> /dev/sda'; 'dd of=/dev/sda' (write to raw disk) matches neither -> today ALLOWs. Evaluator's dd-of=<block-device> rule -> DENY. Red.
Class E setuid persistence: 'install -m 4755' drops a setuid root binary; no pattern covers 'install' today -> ALLOWs. Evaluator's install -m 4xxx (setuid) rule -> DENY. Red.

Class E in-place WRITE to a sensitive path: 'sed -i ... ~/.aws/credentials' mutates credentials; today has no path protection for Bash -> ALLOWs. Evaluator: any write to a sensitive path escalates -> DENY (unambiguous write, not ask). Red.

Class E silent exfil: the curl detector matches only -d/--data followed by [\s=]; '--data-binary' has '-' after --data so it evades, and the credential read is unguarded -> today ALLOWs. Evaluator: sensitive read + egress sink -> DENY (read+egress bypass family, not ask). Red.

Class E: today's chmod -R 777 HITL pattern returns ASK, but under a bypassPermissions/non-interactive controller an ASK auto-resolves to ALLOW, so world-writable recursion on / must DENY. Today's verdict (ask) != expected (deny) -> WRONG -> Red. Evaluator: chmod -R 777 hard-deny.
Canonical bare-root rm: today's /rm\s+-r[f]?\s+\/\s*$/ matches at end-of-string -> DENY today. Evaluator also DENY. Correct both before and after -> green. Regression anchor for the rm-regex path.
Canonical fork bomb: exact BLOCKED_STRINGS literal ':(){ :|:& };:' (survives whitespace normalization) -> DENY today. Evaluator also DENY. Green. Regression anchor for BLOCKED_STRINGS.
Canonical filesystem format: BLOCKED_REGEX /\bmkfs(\.[a-z0-9]+)?\b/ matches 'mkfs.ext4' -> DENY today. Evaluator also DENY. Green. Regression anchor for the mkfs word-boundary regex.
Canonical raw-disk overwrite: exact BLOCKED_STRINGS literal '> /dev/sda' -> DENY today. Evaluator also DENY. Green. Regression anchor for BLOCKED_STRINGS redirect shape.

PROMOTED canonical slot (per the count-check's authorized 'promote one canonical-destructive slot'). Unobfuscated destructive subpath rm: today's rm regexes only catch bare-root / at EOS and /-followed-by-non-letter, so /etc leaks (§4 Bonus finding) -> today ALLOWs. Evaluator DENIES rm -rf on a system path. Red: destructive subpath rm leaks today with zero obfuscation.
Benign directory listing: no BLOCKED/HITL pattern -> null today; evaluator -> null. Correct both before and after -> green. Must-not-deny guard.
Benign test run: no pattern matches -> null today; evaluator -> null. Green. Must-not-deny guard (common agent command).
Benign git query: matches no git HITL pattern (not push --force / reset --hard / clean) -> null today; evaluator -> null. Green.

Benign variable in ARGUMENT position: $HOME is not in command position so no variable-indirection match -> null today; evaluator keeps $HOME/${PWD} in arg position as allow -> null. Green. False-positive guard for env vars as args.

Benign $PWD in argument position (after 'ls '), not command position -> no HITL var-indirection match -> null today; evaluator -> null. Green. False-positive guard: env var as an argument must not escalate.
Benign file read of a non-sensitive path: no pattern -> null today; evaluator -> null (README.md is not a sensitive path). Green. Must-not-deny guard.
Benign recursive grep: no pattern -> null today; evaluator -> null. Green. Must-not-deny guard for a common search command.

Negative-result / no-crash: whitespace-only degenerate input. Today normalizes to a single space, matches nothing -> null. A fail-closed-but-sound evaluator tokenizes to an empty argv (nothing to execute) -> deterministic null (not deny -- there is no command to be destructive). Verdicts agree -> green. Chosen null per the guidance 'a benign one -> null'.

Negative-result / no-crash: deeply-quoted-but-benign. Single quotes make the inner double-quotes and $vars literal; no pattern -> null today. Evaluator's lexer tracks the balanced single-quote span, $vars is inert inside single quotes -> benign echo -> null. Agree -> green. Stresses quote-state tracking without a destructive payload; chosen null (benign).

Negative-result / no-crash: unbalanced-LOOKING bracket that is a quoted regex fragment. The '[' is inside balanced double quotes, so it is a literal grep argument. No pattern -> null today. Evaluator tokenizes the balanced quotes successfully -> benign grep -> null (a scary-looking-but-quoted metacharacter must not false-positive). Agree -> green; chosen null (benign).
